parole.significato: Any of many bulbous plants of the genus Allium, including onions and garlic.
parole.testo: From taxonomic name Allium, from Latin allium.

parole.significato: Any member of the genus Amphiuma of aquatic salamanders.
parole.testo: Borrowed from taxonomic name Amphiuma, from Latin amphi- (“around, both”), and an alteration of Ancient Greek πνεῦμα (pneûma, “breath”).

parole.significato: Any member of the suborder Ankylosauria, herbaceous dinosaurs notable for their armor consisting of bony osteoderms.
parole.testo: From taxonomic name Ankylosauria + -an, equivalent to ankylosaur + -ian, from Ankylosaurus + New Latin -ia, q.v. Compare nodosaurian, derived within English.

parole.significato: Any member of the family Ankylosauridae, ankylosaurians with clublike tails.
parole.testo: From taxonomic name Ankylosauridae, from Ankylosaurus + New Latin -idae (“-id, related to”), from Ancient Greek -ίδης (-ídēs, “-son, son of”). Equivalent to ankylosaur + -id.

parole.significato: Any member of the subfamily Ankylosaurinae, herbaceous dinosaurs closely related to ankylosaurus.
parole.testo: From taxonomic name Ankylosaurinae, from Ankylosaurus + New Latin -inae (“-ine”), equivalent to ankylosaur + -ine.

parole.significato: A strawberry tree, any of the flowering plants in the genus Arbutus.
parole.testo: From taxonomic name Arbutus, from Latin arbutus.

parole.significato: Any of many aromatic flowering plants of the genus Artemisia, including wormwood, sagebrush, and tarragon, often used a…
parole.testo: From taxonomic name Artemisia, from Latin artemisia, from Ancient Greek ἀρτεμισία (artemisía), from Ἄρτεμις (Ártemis, “Artemis, the goddess”).

parole.significato: Any member of the Asclepiadaceae.
parole.testo: From Asclepiad-, the stem of the taxonomic name Asclepias, from Latin asclēpias (stem: asclēpiad-), from Ancient Greek ἀσκληπιάς (asklēpiás) (stem: ἀσκληπιάδ- (asklēpiád-)).

parole.significato: Any plant of the genus Asclepias.
parole.testo: Borrowed from taxonomic name Asclepias.

parole.significato: Synonym of dryopteris: a member of a certain genus of ferns, including the male fern.
parole.testo: A genericized form of taxonomic name Aspidium, from New Latin aspidium (“shield fern”) proposed by Schwartz in Schrader's Journal für die Botanik in 1800, from Ancient Greek ἀσπίς (aspís, “shield”) + -ium.

parole.significato: Any member of the genus Magnapinna of rarely seen squid, characterized by extremely long arms and tentacles, and being…
parole.testo: Calque of taxonomic name Magnapinna, from Latin magna (“big, large”) + pinna (“fin”).

parole.significato: Any single-celled green alga, of the genus Chlorella, found especially in stagnant water; now produced commercially as…
parole.testo: A use as a common noun of the genus name taxonomic name Chlorella, from New Latin chlorella, from chlōrus + -ella (“diminutive”), from Ancient Greek χλωρός (khlōrós, “pale green”).

parole.significato: Any of the genus †Squalicorax of extinct mackerel sharks, known to have lived during the Cretaceous period.
parole.testo: Calque of taxonomic name Squalicorax, which is derived from Latin squalus (“shark”) + Ancient Greek κόραξ (kórax, “raven; crow”).

parole.significato: Any carp of the genus Labeo.
parole.testo: Borrowed from taxonomic name Labeo, from Latin labeō.

parole.significato: Any snail of the genus Nerita, or more generally, of the family Neritidae.
parole.testo: Borrowed from taxonomic name Nerita, from Latin nērīta, from Ancient Greek νηρῑ́της (nērī́tēs, “sea snail”).

parole.significato: A type of deciduous shrub native to the southeastern United States, often cultivated as an ornamental plant, of species…
parole.testo: Partial calque of taxonomic name Hydrangea quercifolia. The specific epithet quercifolia comes from Latin quercus (“oak”) + Latin folia (“leaf”), referring to the leaves' similarity in shape to those of oak trees, which belong to the unrelated genus Quercus.

parole.significato: Any reptile of the order Squamata; a lizard, snake or mosasauroid.
parole.testo: From the taxonomic name Squamata, from Latin squāmātus.

parole.significato: Resembling or characteristic of a unionid.
parole.testo: From taxonomic name Unio (with insertion of -n- after its etymon, Classical Latin ūniō (stem ūniōn-)) + -iform.

parole.significato: Any member of the family Unionidae or its order Unionida of freshwater mussels.
parole.testo: From taxonomic name Unio (with insertion of -n- after its etymon, Classical Latin ūniō (stem ūniōn-)) + -oid. Compare earlier unionid and taxonomic name Unionioda.

parole.significato: Any of the genus Volvox of chlorophytes.
parole.testo: From taxonomic name Volvox, from Latin volvō (“to roll”).

parole.significato: Any member of the genus Zingiber of gingers.
parole.testo: From taxonomic name Zingiber. Doublet of ginger.
